Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers you showed look promising. Our procurement team has a few follow-ups specific to our MSA/order form: because we operate regulated telemedicine endpoints, we need an explicit availability exhibit with: 

- Uptime commitment (regional) and a tolerance carveout for scheduled maintenance windows longer than 2 hours
- Latency SLOs for the 95th/99th token-level response time for the 'chat' route when requests are <=1k tokens
- Clear failure/fallback behavior (regional failover, model variant fallback) and how that maps to credits
- Evidence required for procurement sign-off: SOC2 evidence pointers, telemetry retention period, runbook excerpt that shows RTO/RPO assumptions

I've attached our procurement questionnaire and an illustrative uptime matrix that shows what the buyer is likely to ask for. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:

1) Add an availability exhibit to the order form with the above scoped language,
2) Provide sample evidence (redacted) for SOC2 and an operations runbook excerpt, and
3) Commit to a DocuSign timeline so we can push this through legal by end of month?

If you prefer, we can jump on a 30-minute call early next week to align.

Thanks,
Jordan

Irene / team — draft language and operational notes below. I'm attaching the first pass of the exhibit as a Word doc. Key technical clarifications:

1) Regional uptime: we can offer a 99.95% regional availability target with a scheduled-maintenance carveout. Scheduled maintenance is defined as planned windows >30m and we propose a single, rolling cumulative allowance of 8 hours per quarter; exceptions can be requested for critical upgrades.

2) Latency SLOs: 95th percentile <=350ms for <=1k token chat requests; 99th percentile <=800ms. These are route-level SLOs measured at the Redwood edge before burst queuing. We will include measurement methodology in the exhibit (sampling rates, timing source).

3) Failover and credits: primary -> regional fallback -> model-variant fallback chain. Credits scale by outage duration and impacted token-hours. We have a simple credit table in the draft (see doc).

4) Evidence: we can provide redacted SOC2 sections (control descriptions + test results), a sanitized runbook excerpt showing incident classification and RTO targets, and a telemetry sample (time-series screenshots + aggregated CSV). Telemetry retention for evidence: operationally we keep 90 days of full telemetry, aggregate metrics for 12 months; we can provide extracts per procurement request.

I've attached draft_orderform_exhibit_v1.docx for internal review — it's intentionally conservative on credit exposure; legal may want to narrow tolerances.

-D

Irene / David / Kimberly / Soojin — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. We reviewed the draft_orderform_exhibit_v1.docx internally and have a few small asks:

- Can the scheduled-maintenance allowance be expressed as two windows of up to 4 hours per quarter rather than a rolling 8-hour pool? That will make our change control easier.

If those three items are acceptable, we can route the doc for a clean-signature DocuSign and aim to be signed by next Thursday (09/21). Please confirm and, if agreed, send the final redline so our legal can do a quick compare.
